articles.title: Global Market: Europe’s tech giants emerge as surprise AI winners as enterprise adoption takes off
articles.description: Europe’s established technology companies are emerging as unexpected winners of the AI boom as enterprises move from experimentation to large-scale adoption. Companies such as SAP, Capgemini, Sopra Steria and OVHcloud are benefiting from rising demand for AI integration, cloud infrastructure, governance and data management. Growing concerns around security and data sovereignty are further boosting Europe’s enterprise technology ecosystem.

articles.title: Explained: Why South Korea bought gold after 13 years and what it means for yellow metal investors?

After a thirteen-year hiatus, South Korea's central bank has made a return to gold investing.

articles.title: RBI's status quo on rates to support housing demand, keep real estate sentiment intact: Industry
articles.description: The RBI's decision to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% for the fourth straight review has received a positive response from the real estate sector. Developers and consultants believe stable interest rates will support housing demand, boost buyer confidence and provide better visibility for project planning. However, rising construction costs remain a concern for affordability, especially in mid-income segments.

articles.title: Global Market: BOJ sees stronger inflation ahead, June minutes show

Minutes from the BOJ’s June policy meeting showed growing debate over the pace of monetary tightening, with some members favouring faster rate hikes as inflation pressures remain resilient.

articles.title: Sterlite Tech, HFCL gain 5% each on reports of US ban on Chinese data centre devices
articles.description: Shares of Sterlite Technologies and HFCL rallied 5% each after reports that the US administration is considering restrictions on Chinese data centre equipment imports. The proposed curbs could impact optical transceivers used in AI infrastructure. HFCL’s planned ₹400 crore capacity expansion in optical fibre and cable manufacturing also gains attention amid rising demand from AI, data centres and telecom networks.

articles.title: Nifty can rally to 28,615 by this December in Axis’ bull case scenario. Here’s why

The brokerage remains overweight on BFSI, healthcare and capital goods, while cautioning that global risks and elevated valuations could trigger near-term volatility.

articles.title: QSR stocks near turning point as risk-reward turns favorable, says Motilal Oswal
articles.description: The Indian quick-service restaurant (QSR) sector is entering a favourable phase after a challenging period, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services. The brokerage believes easing valuations, improving operational trends, and long-term consumption growth could support a recovery in QSR stocks. It remains selective in the space and highlights Jubilant FoodWorks, Sapphire Foods India, Westlife Foodworld, and Devyani International as key picks.

articles.title: Molbio Diagnostics IPO to open on August 10, price band set at Rs 768-807
articles.description: Molbio Diagnostics is set to launch its IPO on August 10, 2026, with a price band of Rs 768-807 per share. The Rs 939.70 crore public issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 200 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 739.70 crore by existing shareholders. The molecular diagnostics company plans to use the proceeds to expand R&D infrastructure, manufacturing capabilities, and strengthen its healthcare diagnostics portfolio.
